accuracy.evidence: Checked against the NC Year 1–2 Animals including humans programme of study (animal groups: fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds, mammals; animals have offspring which grow into adults), BBC Bitesize KS1 'How do animals have babies?' and the Natural History Museum pages on monotremes. Every lab animal is placed by the textbook rule: hen, penguin, swan (birds), crocodile and turtle (reptiles), fish, frog (amphibian), ladybird and butterfly (insects) lay eggs; dog, cow, whale, dolphin, elephant and mouse are mammals with live young. The keyIdea says 'most fish' and 'most mammals'; the adult text names the platypus/echidna and live-bearing fish and snakes as exceptions, and the challenge feedback says 'only a very rare few' mammals lay eggs, so no rule is overstated. Frog egg → tadpole and butterfly egg → caterpillar are correct first stages.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented KS1 confusions (Allen, Misconceptions in Primary Science, ch. on animals; PSTT 'animals including humans' guidance): living in water means fish that lay eggs (whale, dolphin, penguin step), size decides it (crocodile, swan, elephant, mouse step; ostrich in the challenge), and every baby is a small copy of its parent (frog egg predicted to hatch 'a tiny frog', caterpillar predicted to become 'a big caterpillar'). Each appears as a prediction, a named wrong-nest message from slip() and a tagged challenge answer.

lab_distinct.evidence: flaghatch is about how the baby starts: an egg nest vs a born-alive blanket, eggs drawn on the canvas that crack open and ask what came out (with hand-drawn frog spawn and tadpole), and a like-mum/looks-different sort. flagbaby matches babies to mothers and names them (lamb, calf) with no egg/live idea; flagcycle orders life-cycle stages round a circle. Swapping labels would not turn it into either. Shingle gate passed.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child discovers the rule from the sorting: a wrong drop on 'born alive' for a crocodile says 'Big animals can lay eggs too', the whale on 'lays eggs' says it is a mammal whose baby drinks milk, and the Big or small step text then names the question to ask (mammal, or bird/reptile/fish/insect). Cracking the frog egg before choosing makes 'tadpole, not tiny frog' a surprise the lab resolves, then the look-alike sort generalises it.

predictions.evidence: Five predictions, each with a tempting wrong answer the lab disproves: crocodile babies 'are born alive' (big, fierce), a frog egg gives 'a tiny frog', a caterpillar grows into 'a big caterpillar', a whale baby 'hatches from an egg' (lives in the sea), and mouse babies 'hatch from tiny eggs' (small). The reveal line on completion says which they picked and why the answer is different.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven rotating questions with three answers each; every wrong answer carries a tag with its own message: 'size' (big animals and all birds lay eggs), 'water' (dolphins and whales are mammals), 'egg' (mammal babies grow inside mum), 'look' (tadpoles and caterpillars change), 'silly' (only plants grow on trees). Answer order rotates per turn so position cannot be learned.

readability.evidence: Kid explanation FK grade 3.4 overall (paragraphs 2.4–4.1), keyIdea 5.0, adult 8.2 (limits 6.5 learner / 5.0 family kid, 9.5 adult). Lab step text is one or two short sentences; canvas labels are two or three words (lays eggs, born alive, looks like mum). The word 'mammal' is introduced with its meaning (babies drink milk from mum) because it is the curriculum term the child needs.

no_filler.evidence: Every kid paragraph carries one fact or rule with named examples; the adult text gives the curriculum link, the biology with exceptions, three named mistakes and what each lab step does. No filler phrase matched; the content gate's 12% duplicate check passed against lesson 174 Animals and their babies and 539 life cycles.

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 screenshots in both themes for every step (shots/hatch-phone-t0/t1, mid-hatch): the card, the egg and the two 'lays eggs' / 'born alive' zones fit at 390 px with no clipping, feedback wraps to two lines, sorted animals line up inside each zone, and every answer is a 56 px button under the canvas (class young). Fixed during review: the hatched babies row was not drawn once all eggs had hatched.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs: axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean on desktop and iPhone 13 in light and dark, no console errors, all 5 tasks complete with Show me. Every drag or tap on the canvas has a button twin with an aria-label naming the animal ('A whale baby is born alive'); the canvas aria-label and the live region repeat each feedback line; the challenge feedback is a role=status region.
